name: Hail Damage Assessment
intro: Welcome to Module 2, Hail Damage Assessment, I'm excited to have you on board. In this module, we're going to dive into the world of hail damage, and by the end of it, you'll be able to identify signs of hail damage on various roofing materials, from asphalt shingles to metal roofs. You'll learn impact assessment techniques that'll help you determine the extent of the damage, and most importantly, you'll know how to document that damage for insurance claims. This is a critical skill for any roofing professional, and I'm confident that with the knowledge and skills you'll gain in this module, you'll be able to tackle even the toughest hail damage assessments with confidence. So let's get started, I'm looking forward to guiding you through this module and helping you take your skills to the next level.

concepts.script:
Here's a 90-second video script on Hail Damage Identification:

"Hello, I'm Agnes, your roofing training instructor. Today, we're going to talk about identifying hail damage on roofs. Hail damage can be tricky to spot, but with a few simple tips, you'll be a pro in no time.

When hail hits a shingle, it creates a circular dent or dimple. Think of it like a coin being pressed into the shingle. This dent can be hard to see, but look closely and you'll notice granule loss around the impacted area. The granules may be missing or loose, exposing the fiberglass mat beneath.

Let's take a look at this example. See how the granules are missing around this dent? And if we look closer, we can see the fiberglass mat underneath. This is a clear sign of hail damage.

Another thing to look for is bruising patterns. When hail hits a shingle, it can cause the asphalt to bruise, creating a dark spot or a pattern of spots. This bruising can be subtle, but it's a key indicator of hail damage.

So, to recap: when identifying hail damage, look for circular dents or dimples, granule loss, and bruising patterns. And remember, the key is to inspect the roof carefully, taking your time to examine each shingle. With practice, you'll be able to spot hail damage like a pro. Let's get out there and start inspecting!"

"Welcome to today's roofing training on Impact Assessment. When it comes to hail damage, determining the severity is crucial for a proper repair. Let's break it down into three key factors: size, density of impacts, and affected areas. 

Imagine you're inspecting a roof after a hail storm. You notice some damaged shingles, but how do you know if it's just cosmetic or something more serious? That's where test squares come in. By examining a small, defined area, you can get a better sense of the damage. 

For example, if you have a test square with 5 impacts, each about 1 inch in diameter, that's a different story than having 20 impacts, each about 0.5 inches in diameter. The size and density of impacts will help you determine the severity of the damage. 

Proper documentation is also essential. Take photos, notes, and measurements of the affected areas. This will help you create a clear picture of the damage and ensure that your assessment is accurate. 

Let's look at a real-life example. Suppose you have a roof with moderate hail damage on the south-facing slope, but the rest of the roof is unaffected. Your impact assessment would focus on that specific area, taking into account the size and density of impacts, as well as the overall condition of the shingles. 

By following these steps and using test squares, you'll be able to provide a thorough and accurate impact assessment, ensuring that the repair is done right and the roof is secure. Remember, a thorough assessment is key to a successful repair. Take your time, be thorough, and document everything."
